evidence: Cic. Univ. 4: corporeum et aspectābile itemque tractābile (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s word in his Timaeus for what is made of matter, which can be seen and touched; Lucretius uses it often of bodies and things. The opposite, immaterial, is incorporālis (Sen.) or quod corpore caret.

terms.gloss: that can be touched or handled; tangible
terms.comment: Also, of things and people, pliant and manageable (Cic. Lael. 48).

sources: Lewis & Short: corporeus · Lewis & Short: tractabilis
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. physical, material.
